text:
QUOTE: With a callback and no allow match, the call is approved, and the callback is only a notification.
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer says the approval step grants a call not on the allow list when a callback is registered, but it never concludes that a tool matching neither list runs. Without a callback it says such a call is denied, and its closing questions cast the gap as a callback-denial and ordering problem. It never states that default-allow is the effective posture at the blocking gate.
